description: News updates and supporting documents relating to the government’s ambitious programme of local government reorganisation in England.

details.body:
About Local Government Reorganisation

Nearly a third of England’s population, around 20 million people, live in areas with two-tier local government with services and functions split across county and district council.

This slows down decision making and delivery, leads to fragmented public services, sees money wasted on duplication and makes it unclear who is responsible for what and where accountability lies.

Our ambition is to simplify local government, by ending the two-tier system and establishing new single-tier unitary councils.

This is a once in a generation reform and our vision is clear: stronger local councils empowered across local services, equipped to drive economic growth, improve local public services and empower their communities.

Timeline

16 December 2024

The English Devolution White Paper was published. This set out the government’s vision for simpler local government structures.

The Minister of State for Local Government and English Devolution wrote to all councils in remaining two-tier areas and neighbouring small unitaries to set out plans for a joint programme of devolution and local government reorganisation.

5 February 2025

​The Minister of State for Local Government and English Devolution issued a statutory invitation to all councils in two-tier areas and neighbouring small unitary councils to develop proposals for unitary local government as well as updating on decisions on requests to postpone local elections. 

​Councils were asked to produce interim plans and submit these to government by 21 March 2025.

24 March 2025

A  written ministerial statement was made to Parliament. This set out that the government had received responses from all 21 invited areas.

It also announced that £7.6 million will be made available in the form of Local Government Reorganisation Proposal Development Contributions, to be split across these 21 areas. 

8 May 2025

​Councils in Surrey submitted final proposals for unitary councils in their area.

3 June 2025

A written ministerial statement was made to Parliament. This set out how the Proposal Development Contributions would be allocated, the amount that each area would receive, and the method for receiving that payment.

The statement also confirmed that each area has now received feedback on their interim plans and that a summary of that feedback has been published.  

17 June 2025

A written ministerial statement was made to Parliament about the statutory consultation on proposals for unitary local government in Surrey.

26 September 2025

Final proposals for local government reorganisation in their area were submitted by councils in:

  • East Sussex and Brighton
  • Essex, Southend-on-Sea and Thurrock
  • Hampshire, Isle of Wight, Portsmouth and Southampton
  • Norfolk
  • Suffolk
  • West Sussex

28 October 2025

A written ministerial statement was made to Parliament, outlining the decision to implement 2 unitary councils in Surrey.

19 November 2025

​A written ministerial statement was made to Parliament about the statutory consultations on proposals for unitary local government made by councils in 6 areas.

Consultations were published for:

  • East Sussex and Brighton and Hove, and West Sussex
  • Essex, Southend-on-Sea and Thurrock
  • Hampshire, Isle of Wight, Portsmouth and Southampton
  • Norfolk and Suffolk

The Minister of State for Local Government and Homelessness also wrote to leaders of all councils engaged with local government reorganisation proposals about the importance of the Publicity Code.

28 November 2025

Final proposals for local government reorganisation across 14 areas were submitted by councils in:

  • Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
  • Derbyshire and Derby  
  • Devon, Plymouth and Torbay 
  • Gloucestershire 
  • Hertfordshire 
  • Kent and Medway 
  • Lancashire, Blackpool and Blackburn with Darwen 
  • Leicestershire, Leicester and Rutland 
  • Lincolnshire, North Lincolnshire and Northeast Lincolnshire 
  • Nottinghamshire and Nottingham 
  • Oxfordshire 
  • Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent 
  • Warwickshire 
  • Worcestershire

The letters on the following dates have now been superseded by the Secretary of State’s letter to councils on 16 February 2026:

  • 18 December 2025
  • 15 January 2026
  • 19 January 2026
  • 22 January 2026
  • 29 January 2026

18 December 2025

The Minister of State for Local Government and Homelessness wrote to council leaders in local government reorganisation areas holding elections in May 2026.

The letter invites councils to set out their views on:

  • the potential postponement of their local election in May 2026
  • whether doing this would allow them to better deliver local government reorganisation

A written ministerial statement was also made.

15 January 2026

Deadline for representations from councils in local government reorganisation areas holding local elections in May 2026 on the potential postponement of local elections and whether this would release essential capacity to deliver local government reorganisation.

19 January 2026

The Secretary of State wrote to 4 councils, asking for clarity on their position in relation to the potential postponement of local elections in May 2026.

22 January 2026

Following the letters and written ministerial statement of 18 December 2025, the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government wrote to council leaders to confirm the decisions made on the postponement of local elections in local government reorganisation areas.

A written ministerial statement was also made.

29 January 2026

The Secretary of State wrote to Pendle Borough and Essex County Council leaders after having received further representations in respect of the timing of their local elections.

5 February 2026

A written ministerial statement was made to Parliament about the statutory consultations on proposals for unitary local government made by councils in 14 areas.

Consultations were published for:

  • Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
  • Derbyshire and Derby
  • Devon, Plymouth and Torbay 
  • Gloucestershire
  • Hertfordshire
  • Kent and Medway
  • Lancashire, Blackburn with Darwen and Blackpool
  • Leicestershire, Leicester and Rutland
  • Lincolnshire, North Lincolnshire and North East Lincolnshire
  • Nottinghamshire and Nottingham
  • Oxfordshire
  • Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent
  • Warwickshire
  • Worcestershire

16 February 2026

The Secretary of State wrote to council leaders in local government reorganisation areas about the proposed postponement of local elections in May 2026.

9 March 2026

The Minister of State for Local Government and Homelessness signed the Surrey (Structural Changes) Order 2026 implementing the decision of the Secretary of State to abolish the existing district and county councils in Surrey and create 2 new councils, East Surrey Council and West Surrey Council, from 1 April 2027.

25 March 2026

A written ministerial statement was made to Parliament, outlining the decision to implement:

  • 5 unitary councils in Essex, Southend-on-Sea and Thurrock
  • 5 unitary councils (known locally as option 1A) in Hampshire, Isle of Wight, Portsmouth and Southampton
  • 3 unitary councils in Norfolk
  • 3 unitary councils in Suffolk

The written ministerial statement also provided an update on local government reorganisation in East Sussex and Brighton and Hove, and West Sussex.

12 May 2026

Two consultations on potential modifications to local government reorganisation proposals were published for:

  • East Sussex and Brighton and Hove
  • West Sussex

16 July 2026

​A written ministerial statement was made to Parliament, and the Secretary of State wrote to areas outlining the decision to implement the following proposals in local government reorganisation areas.

One unitary council will be implemented in:

  • Gloucestershire

Two unitary councils will be implemented in:

  • ​Derbyshire and Derby
  • East Sussex and Brighton and Hove
  • Leicestershire, Leicester and Rutland
  • Nottinghamshire and Nottingham
  • Staffordshire and Stoke on Trent
  • Warwickshire
  • Worcestershire

Three unitary councils will be implemented in:

  • Oxfordshire

Four unitary councils will be implemented in:

  • ​Devon, Plymouth and Torbay
  • Hertfordshire
  • Kent and Medway
  • Lancashire, Blackburn with Darwen and Blackpool
  • ​Lincolnshire, North Lincolnshire and Northeast Lincolnshire

The Secretary of State also wrote to provide an update on local government reorganisation to leaders in:

  • Cambridgeshire and Peterborough
  • West Sussex

This was also reflected in the written ministerial statement.

The Secretary of State also wrote to all areas undergoing local government reorganisation to issue guidance on:

  • sector support
  • staffing issues
  • adult social care, public health and children’s services.

7 September 2026

An oral statement was made to Parliament by the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government.

This statement announced the withdrawal of the current decisions for:

  • Essex, Southend-on-Sea and Thurrock
  • Hampshire, Isle of Wight, Portsmouth and Southampton
  • Norfolk
  • Suffolk

It also announced a rapid review of the local government reorganisation programme. This includes decisions taken in July 2026 and the 2 outstanding areas awaiting decisions. This does not impact the decision taken in Surrey

The Minister for Local Government, Devolution and Regional Growth also wrote to leaders of all local government reorganisation areas to inform them.

29 October 2026

​An oral statement was made to parliament by the Minister for Local Government, Devolution and Regional Growth and a written ministerial statement laid in the house. This statement updated parliament on the review of the programme announced in September.

The Minister for Local Government, Devolution and Regional Growth also wrote to 5 areas concerning decisions he and the Secretary of State were minded to take, subject to a representations process and parliamentary approval before final decisions.

​The Minister for Local Government, Devolution and Regional Growth also wrote to:

  • 9 areas confirming the withdrawal of their July 2026 decisions
  • 4 areas where decisions were withdrawn in September 2026
  • 2 areas where decisions have not yet received responses

The letters provided a programme update and detail on next steps for the review

The written ministerial statement also included information on funding, city status and ceremonial matters. 

The current position on local government reorganisation 

​Five areas have new minded-to decisions, subject to representations before final decisions. These are:

  • East Sussex and Brighton and Hove
  • Gloucestershire
  • Oxfordshire, including the adjoining area of West Berkshire
  • Warwickshire
  • Worcestershire

Fifteen areas remain under review. Surrey is unaffected, with its new councils going live in April 2027.
